Self-cited Article Title: Zhang, Z.C., Lin, X.Y., Shan, S.N. and Yin, Z. (2023), “Big data-assisted urban governance: forecasting social events with a periodicity by employing different time series algorithms”, Library Hi Tech, Early Access, doi: 10.1108/lht-12-2022-0550.
Citation Location: Introduction
Citation Content: Relying on the spatiotemporal big data platform and AI technology for statistical analysis and simulation algorithm, it helps to diagnose the urban operation status in real-time and predict the future development trend of urban space g (Jiang et al., 2021; Verdouw et al., 2021; Opoku et al., 2021). Since 2020, many researchers have begun to focus on public crisis governance in digital twin cities. In particular, the emergence of COVID-19 has demonstrated the significant advantages of digital twin technology in responding to urban public crisis events. For example, Beijing uses the digital twin city platform to accurately count the number of temperature measurements, abnormalities, and cumulative testing. It uses unity3D scenes for real-time monitoring and control of fixed areas. It uses contactless robots to complete public services such as disinfection, temperature measurement, cleaning, and delivery to prevent epidemic leakage (Wang et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023). An in-depth study is necessary since public crisis governance in digital twin cities is a relatively new topic. Therefore, this paper aims to explore the influencing factors and implementation paths of public crisis governance in digital twin cities to improve its governance performance. For this purpose, Section 2 provides a review of the existing literature. Section 3 describes the methodology used in this research. Section 4 shows the results obtained according to the methodology and discusses them. Finally, Section 5 presents the conclusions of this paper.

Citation Location: Discussion
Citation Content: First, this paper presents a comprehensive model of virtual live encountering information adoption from immersion experience. The findings indicate that immersion experience has a positive effect on users encountering information adoption, perceived usefulness, trust, and commitment. This was determined through structural equation empirical research. The findings align with those of previous studies, including those by Cheng (2023a, b), Lin et al. (2017), and Cheng (2021).
